translationRepairs: In Jianwu he again went out as staff officer to Pingxi general Xiao Yaoqin and Nankang prefect.
In Jianwu he again went out as staff officer to Pingxi general Xiao Yaoqin and Nanjun prefect.
s0010 南郡太守 names the commandery 南郡 (Nanjun); Nankang is 南康 and is not in the Chinese.
In the Jianwu era he again went out as staff officer to Pingxi general Xiao Yaoqin and prefect of Nankang.
In the Jianwu era he again went out as staff officer to Pingxi general Xiao Yaoqin and prefect of Nanjun.
The literal likewise renders 南郡 as Nankang; Nanjun is the correct place name for 南郡.
s0052 元起，南郡人 states Yuanqi was a man of 南郡 (Nanjun), not Nankang.
Yuanqi was a man of Nankang commandery.
Yuanqi was a man of Nanjun commandery.
The literal of s0052 likewise misreads 南郡 as Nankang; Nanjun restores the Chinese place name.
When Lijian had held Nankang he had always looked down on Yuanqi.
When Lijian had held Nanjun he had always looked down on Yuanqi.
s0053 季連爲南郡之時 refers to Lijian’s tenure over 南郡 (Nanjun), not Nankang.
When Lijian had held Nankang he had always looked down on Yuanqi.
When Lijian had held Nanjun he had always looked down on Yuanqi.
The literal of s0053 has the same 南郡→Nankang error; Nanjun matches the Chinese.
In year two's second month Gaozu sent chief secretary Zhao Jingyue to announce an edict accepting Lijian's surrender; Lijian bared his torso and begged pardon.
In year two's first month Gaozu sent chief secretary Zhao Jingyue to announce an edict accepting Lijian's surrender; Lijian bared his torso and begged pardon.
s0076 二年正月 is the first month of year two; 正月 is not the second month.
In the second month of year two Gaozu sent chief secretary Zhao Jingyue to announce an edict accepting Lijian's surrender; Lijian bared his torso and begged pardon.
In the first month of year two Gaozu sent chief secretary Zhao Jingyue to announce an edict accepting Lijian's surrender; Lijian bared his torso and begged pardon.
The literal likewise turns 正月 into “second month”; “first month” is required by the Chinese.
Qi Lord of Anding Zijing held southern Yang and kept many troops for self-defense.
Qi Prince of Anlu Zijing held Southern Yanzhou and kept many troops for self-defense.
s0098 齊安陸王子敬爲南兗州 names Prince of Anlu Zijing and Southern Yanzhou; “Anding” and “southern Yang” misread 安陸王 and 南兗州.
Qi Lord of Anding Zijing held southern Yang and kept many troops about him for self-defense.
Qi Prince of Anlu Zijing held Southern Yanzhou and kept many troops about him for self-defense.
The literal of s0098 has the same Anding/southern Yang errors; Prince of Anlu and Southern Yanzhou match 安陸王 and 南兗州.

When Bozhi arrived he was made bearer of staff, area commander of Western Xinyang, Pacification North general, and Western Xinyang inspector, Marquis of Yongxin with a fief of one thousand households.
When Bozhi arrived he was made bearer of staff, area commander of Western Yuzhou, Pacification North general, and Western Yuzhou inspector, Marquis of Yongxin with a fief of one thousand households.
s0203 都督西豫州諸軍事 and 西豫州刺史 name Western Yuzhou (西豫州), not Western Xinyang.

When Bozhi arrived he was made Bearer of Staff, Area Commander of Western Xinyang military affairs, Pacification North General, and Western Xinyang Inspector, Marquis of Yongxin county, fief of one thousand households.

When Bozhi arrived he was made Bearer of Staff, Area Commander of Western Yuzhou military affairs, Pacification North General, and Western Yuzhou Inspector, Marquis of Yongxin county, fief of one thousand households.
The literal likewise misreads 西豫州 as Western Xinyang; Western Yuzhou restores the Chinese province name.
Chu Chuo was in Wei, and the Wei court wished to promote and employ him.
Chu Wei was in Wei, and the Wei court wished to promote and employ him.
s0207 names 褚緭; 緭 is read Wei, and Chu Chuo invents a different reading of the same personal name.
Chu Chuo was in Wei; the Wei wished to promote and employ him.
Chu Wei was in Wei; the Wei wished to promote and employ him.
The literal of s0207 likewise has Chu Chuo for 褚緭; Chu Wei is the correct romanization of that name.
The historian writes: Liu Jilian had a literary man's polish, yet could not save himself—as habit in troubled times will do.
The historian writes: Liu Lijian had a literary man's polish, yet could not save himself—as habit in troubled times will do.
s0211 names 劉季連, whom the chapter elsewhere consistently romanizes as Liu Lijian; Liu Jilian is an inconsistent spelling of the same person.
The historian says: Liu Jilian had the small refinements of a literary official, yet could not preserve himself—such is growing accustomed to disorder.
The historian says: Liu Lijian had the small refinements of a literary official, yet could not preserve himself—such is growing accustomed to disorder.
The literal of s0211 likewise uses Liu Jilian for 劉季連; Liu Lijian matches the chapter’s established romanization.

At that time Shiwen'an of Kuaiji, styled Shouxiu, lived in seclusion practicing courtesy, had replaced Lijian as Left Director, gone out as Jiangxia interior governor, then replaced him again as Censor-in-Chief—and he and Lijian were friends.

At that time Shi Wen'an of Kuaiji, styled Shouxiu, lived in seclusion practicing courtesy, had replaced Lijian as Left Director, gone out as Jiangxia interior governor, then replaced him again as Censor-in-Chief—and he and Lijian were friends.
s0046 石文安 is surname 石 plus given name 文安 (Shi Wen'an); fusing them as Shiwen'an mis-segments the personal name.
